items.title: 12.12 Role of sulfur in the organic synthesis of drugs, dyes and fragrances

blocks.text: Carbon-sulfur bonds occur in a wide range of compounds with biological, pharmaceutical and material properties. They form a large number of organic compounds containing functional groups such as thiols or mercaptans (R-SH), thioethers (R-S-R), sulfoxides (R-S(=O)-R) and sulfones (R-SO2-R). The next three topics give examples in drugs, dyes and odorants.

blocks.prompt: What is the importance of disulfide bridges (exercise Q.2m)?
blocks.explanation: A disulfide bridge, S-S, forms when two thiol groups are oxidised; in proteins it links cysteine units within or between chains and holds the folded structure together, as sulfur cross-links hold vulcanised rubber. Such bridges stabilise enzymes, antibodies and the keratin of hair.

items: C-S bonds give thiols (R-SH), thioethers, sulfoxides, sulfones; used in drugs, dyes and fragrances.
